practices.practice: Create a single MongoClient and reuse it as a process-wide singleton; initialize/connect once and do not create a client per request.

Tune connection pool parameters by application context: small pools (maxPoolSize 3–5) for serverless, larger pools (50+) for long-running OLTP servers, set minPoolSize and maxIdleTimeMS appropriately.
Always use TLS (tls=true) for connections to Azure DocumentDB and do not disable certificate validation in production.
Prefer Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) + RBAC or per-app least-privilege users instead of reusing an admin/master credential; use managed identities where supported.
Respect BSON/Document size limits: plan schemas to stay well under the 16 MB document size ceiling and split or spill large growing arrays into child/side collections.
Store timestamps using the database Date/ISODate type (UTC) and index date fields when they are used for time-based queries or aggregations.
Design compound indexes using the ESR rule (Equality → Sort → Range) and prefer a single well-shaped compound index over multiple overlapping single-field indexes.

Use partial indexes (partialFilterExpression) to index only the subset of documents your query filters on to reduce index size and write cost (e.g., index only published rows or a predicate the app always supplies).
Use server-side aggregation pipelines for rollups (e.g., $group with $dateToString or $dateTrunc to bucket by month) so the grouping runs in the database and only summarized results are returned.
Enable diagnostic settings and slow-query logs and analyse them in Log Analytics to find the top expensive queries and feed those back into index design.

Azure DocumentDB provides native vector indexes (`cosmosSearch`) with multiple backends; pick kind by scale (vector-ivf under ~10k, vector-hnsw up to ~50k, vector-diskann for large production workloads) and tune dimensions/similarity/parameters accordingly.

Full-text search in Azure DocumentDB uses createSearchIndexes + the $search aggregation stage (BM25) rather than the community $text operator; build search indexes with explicit mappings and analyzers.
Azure DocumentDB does not support retryable writes in the cluster connection string by default — set retryWrites=false in the connection string when advised by the service documentation.

Enable retryReads at the driver level for transient read failures and implement application-level retries with exponential backoff and jitter for retryable error codes; only retry idempotent operations automatically.
Enable HA (in-region with availability zones) for production clusters to achieve the service SLA (99.99%); add cross-region replicas for higher SLA and DR planning.
For local development use the DocumentDB Gateway image with TLS and env-driven configuration (SKIP_INIT_DATA, INIT_DATA_PATH) and keep seed scripts idempotent and under version control.

Design shard keys only when needed: default to single-shard unless storage or throughput will exceed one physical shard's budget, and choose shard-key based on read- or write- patterns to avoid hot partitions.

Monitor query performance with explain('executionStats') and index usage ($indexStats) to detect COLLSCANs, high keysExamined/nReturned ratios, and blocking in-memory sorts and then add or reshape indexes to fix them.
Seed scripts should be idempotent (use upsert or conditional writes) and not run automatically in production; keep them versioned and ordered for local/dev initialization.
Use customer-managed keys (CMK) for encryption at rest for regulated workloads and prefer Private Endpoint / firewall rules to disable public network access for production clusters.
Normalize embeddings when using cosine similarity and store the embedding dimensions and model id alongside vectors; consider product quantization or fp16 to reduce vector-index memory footprint.

Do not rely on a RU/sec autoscale model in guidance-heavy documentation for Azure DocumentDB; capacity/tiers are expressed as compute tiers (M10, M30, ...) and pick a tier/HA options appropriate to expected workload.
When using the driver, only retry idempotent operations automatically; implement application-level retries with exponential backoff/jitter and handle 429 (throttling) explicitly.
Avoid long-running multi-document transactions where possible; prefer single-document atomic updates and keep any required multi-document transactions short to limit contention and cross-shard cost.
Create a compound index on { date: 1, category: 1 } (or the appropriate ESR-ordered variant) to accelerate monthly-spend aggregations grouped by month and category.

Enable and inspect index usage with db.collection.aggregate([{$indexStats:{}}]) and adjust index-count budgets; prefer 5–15 useful indexes per collection and remove unused indexes safely via hide/drop lifecycle.

When building aggregation pipelines, run explain('executionStats') on the pipeline (or via MCP explain_operation) to measure totalDocsExamined, totalKeysExamined and identify COLLSCANs or blocking SORT stages before changing indexes.
Use environment variables and Key Vault references for secrets in deployment templates; never hardcode admin passwords in parameters files committed to source control.
If you build a local DocumentDB gateway for development, keep prod/dev parity by using the same index and seed scripts and treat SKIP_INIT_DATA as true in non-local environments.
Create explicit search analyzers for prefix and ID matching (keyword+lowerCase+asciiFolding+edgeGram) when you want case-insensitive or prefix-based full-text search behavior.

Several LLM-specific practices (batching, audit logging, PII redaction, strict prompt-output validation) had no explicit Azure DocumentDB documentation in the skills I loaded; I listed those prior beliefs as 'prior_knowledge_only' and recorded the searches attempted.
